blocks.text: 1. Chat with PDFs
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061191-829747909.png

Scaling Strategies closed the Production RAG module by covering how a system grows to handle load. Chat with PDFs, a complete RAG system design for conversational question answering over uploaded documents, opens this final module by combining specific techniques from across the entire course into one concrete, working system.

The system draws on chunking strategy, embedding and indexing choices, retrieval scoping, citation formatting, conversation memory, and faithfulness guardrails, each covered separately earlier, now working together as a single pipeline.
2. The Design Problem's Scope
The four stage pipeline from Naive RAG forms the backbone here: a user uploads one or more PDF documents and asks natural language questions about their content.
The system must ground every answer in the actual uploaded text, not general knowledge.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Design requirement","Technique it draws on"],"rows":[["Ground answers in uploaded text","Faithfulness and citation prompting"],["Handle irregular PDF structure","Recursive chunking"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Choosing A Chunking Strategy For PDF Content

blocks.alt: Choosing A Chunking Strategy For PDF Content
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061191-423344507.png
Recursive chunking, introduced in Chunking, fits PDFs particularly well because PDF content often has irregular structure, making it a safer default than fixed size splitting.
Preserving paragraph and section boundaries matters more here than in cleanly structured text.
4. Embedding And Indexing The Uploaded Document
Since embedding is expensive and deterministic, as covered in Embedding Cache, each uploaded document's chunks get embedded once at upload time and stored in a per-session or per-user index.
The index scope stays narrow: just this document, not the entire knowledge base.
5. Retrieval Scoped To The Current Document

blocks.alt: Retrieval Scoped To The Current Document
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061192-9851781.png
Using the metadata filtering technique from Vector Databases, retrieval must be filtered to only the currently active document, not chunks from any other uploaded file.
A metadata tag identifying the source document is what makes that scoping possible.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metadata field","What it enables"],"rows":[["Source document ID","Filtering retrieval to the active document"],["Page number","Citing the exact page an answer came from"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Citing Page Numbers In The Generated Answer

blocks.alt: Citing Page Numbers In The Generated Answer
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061392-891161387.png
Building on the citation format consistency covered in Citation Prompting, each chunk retains its original page number as metadata, carried through into the generated citation.
A user can jump directly to the exact page an answer was drawn from.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A chunk tagged with page fourteen at ingestion time carries that page number all the way through retrieval into the final citation, letting the user click straight to the source.

blocks.text: 7. Handling Questions About Multiple Uploaded Files

blocks.alt: Handling Questions About Multiple Uploaded Files
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061392-504001666.png
As Chain Of Thought notes for multi-hop questions, a question spanning several uploaded documents needs retrieval widened to all of them, not just one.
The metadata filter scope expands or narrows based on what the user actually asked.
8. Conversational Follow-Up Questions Need Memory
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061392-686489915.png
Short-term memory within one conversation, covered in Memory, becomes essential here: a follow-up question like 'what about the second one' only makes sense with the prior turn's context.
Conversation history must be threaded into each new retrieval and generation call.
9. Guarding Against Questions The Uploaded Document Does Not Answer

blocks.alt: Guarding Against Questions The Uploaded Document Does Not Answer
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061392-968223673.png
As Faithfulness establishes, a claim with no supporting context counts as unfaithful, so a question with no answer anywhere in the uploaded document must be declined, not guessed.
System prompting must explicitly instruct the model to say so rather than answer from general knowledge.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates document-scoped retrieval, page citation, and declining an unanswerable question.

code.content:
chunks = [
    {"doc_id": "resume.pdf", "page": 1, "text": "Experience includes five years as a backend engineer."},
    {"doc_id": "resume.pdf", "page": 2, "text": "Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science."},
    {"doc_id": "contract.pdf", "page": 3, "text": "Payment terms: net thirty days from invoice date."},
]

def retrieve_scoped(query, active_doc_id):
    # retrieval scoped to the currently active document only
    return [c for c in chunks if c["doc_id"] == active_doc_id]

def generate_with_citation(query, retrieved):
    # citation includes the source page number
    matches = [c for c in retrieved if any(w in c["text"].lower() for w in query.lower().split())]
    if not matches:
        return "I could not find an answer to that in this document."
    top = matches[0]
    return f"{top['text']} (Source: {top['doc_id']}, page {top['page']})"

print("Chat with PDFs example:")
scoped = retrieve_scoped("education degree", "resume.pdf")
print(generate_with_citation("education degree", scoped))

print()
scoped = retrieve_scoped("what is the refund policy", "resume.pdf")
print(generate_with_citation("what is the refund policy", scoped))

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the education question answered with a page citation from resume.pdf, while the unrelated refund policy question is correctly declined rather than guessed.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Retrieving from every uploaded document instead of scoping to the one the user is actively asking about.
Losing page number metadata during chunking, making citations impossible to generate.
Answering a question from general knowledge when the uploaded document never actually covers it.
Forgetting to thread conversation history into follow-up questions that depend on prior turns.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Chat with PDFs grounds every answer in the actual uploaded document, not general knowledge.
Recursive chunking handles PDF content's often irregular structure better than fixed size splitting.
Each document's chunks are embedded and indexed narrowly, scoped to that document or session.
A source document metadata tag scopes retrieval to only the currently active file.
Page number metadata carried through to generation enables precise, clickable citations.
A question spanning multiple uploaded files needs the retrieval filter widened accordingly.
Conversation history must be threaded into follow-up questions that depend on prior turns.
A question the uploaded document does not answer must be declined, never guessed from general knowledge.
